## Review summary

Created with AI, based on recent reviews

Considering 260 reviews, most reviewers were unhappy with their experience overall. Consumers frequently reported receiving defective exercise machines that broke down quickly, suffered from frustrating screen failures, or arrived with missing and completely non-functional components. Buyers also struggled to reach helpful support teams, facing long communication delays and severe difficulties when attempting to secure necessary repairs or financial refunds.

Some reviewers were happy with the equipment, praising the smooth performance, responsive service agents, and exceptionally helpful assistance they received during resolution processes. A few people also mentioned the durable build quality, comfortable designs, and the highly engaging workout programs available through the interactive digital platform.See more

[**False promises**](https://www.trustpilot.com/reviews/6ab936b226ac6e26f05b80aa)

I’m very disappointed with my experience trying to purchase a treadmill from NordicTrack.

I initially reached out over a week ago and spoke with Kenney. I explained that timing was extremely important to me and that I needed the treadmill delivered by the end of the following week. I specifically expressed my concerns before placing the order, and I was assured that the order would be pushed through, given higher priority, and expedited.

Unfortunately, that never happened.

After reading all these negative reviews about the equipment issues maybe I’m glad I went with another brand.

After placing the order, I contacted NordicTrack several more times and spoke with multiple representatives who seemed to have no idea what was going on with my order or the expedited delivery I had been promised. I was then asked to provide a utility bill to verify my address, and from that point the experience only became more frustrating.

I continued reaching out for updates, but nobody could give me a clear answer. Instead, I kept being offered small 5% discounts on various things I didn’t need or want. I wasn’t looking for discounts—I simply wanted the treadmill delivered within the timeframe I had been assured it would be.

After more than a week of getting nowhere, I finally canceled my order yesterday and purchased a treadmill from another company. They are delivering it the very next day.

The most frustrating part is that this entire experience could have been avoided with honest communication from the beginning. If expedited delivery wasn’t possible, just tell me that. Don’t promise a customer something to secure the sale and then leave them chasing answers afterward.

NordicTrack may make good equipment, but this purchasing experience and the lack of communication were extremely disappointing.

[**Two NordicTrack products/ Treadmill NordicTrack EXP 14i,**](https://www.trustpilot.com/reviews/6aa82d6375893c76f747cc42)

Two NordicTrack products, two major early failures—and little loyalty recognition

I purchased my NordicTrack EXP 14i treadmill in December 2022. It has received relatively limited use, yet the incline system has already failed and is now stuck at 12%. Calibration and a factory reset did not correct the problem.

Throughout much of this period, I continued paying for an iFIT membership, even though the treadmill was not heavily used. I also own a NordicTrack bike that required a complete screen replacement after only two years.

Given my ownership of two NordicTrack products and my continuing iFIT payments, I expected meaningful customer-loyalty consideration when discussing a replacement treadmill, giving them a chance to redeem themselves. NordicTrack offered 30% off list price and 50% off delivery and haul-away. However, because substantial public discounts were already available, the actual additional loyalty value was limited.

I would have prefered to remain a NordicTrack customer, but experiencing significant problems with two separate products after relatively short periods raises legitimate concerns about long-term reliability. A more appropriate resolution would have helped me reconsider NordicTrack.

I hope NordicTrack/iFIT reviews this situation and provides a resolution that recognizes both the premature equipment failures and my history as a customer.

[**Do Not Buy!**](https://www.trustpilot.com/reviews/6a91ee73d0680dd7b73c7176)

Do not buy. They will not stand behind what they sell!

I bought a NordicTrack commercial-grade treadmill a few years ago (3) because I wanted something that would last. That was the whole point of paying more. It was set up in my home and has never been moved since. Original cord, no modifications, and honestly barely used because after the problems started, I never fully trusted it.

The console is now completely dead. Black screen, no power, no response. This is the second time this exact failure has happened. I tried multiple troubleshooting with the online service.

Here's what the company told me, in order:

My machine is out of warranty, so the repair is entirely on me. Fine, I expected that. They only give a few years anyways, unlike like others that back their products with 20yrs warranty like AVIRON, which I think you should check out.

The proper next step is an on-site technician diagnostic. So I asked for an estimate.

Then: there are no technicians available in my area at all. The step they'd just recommended was never an option. Go find your own repair person.

Then the real answer: the console is discontinued. They don't sell it. Their suggestion was that I search third-party parts sites myself and hope someone has one with no guarantee it fixes anything.

Any part I did buy from them would carry a 90-day warranty. Ninety days, on a "commercial grade" machine.

Then I was handed to Sales to discuss upgrading. And the special discount for the loyal customer whose machine had just been declared unrepairable? 30% off MSRP which is their current Labor Day sale. The identical promotion any stranger gets by clicking an ad. That's not goodwill; that's a sales pitch in a customer-service costume.

The frame, motor, deck, and belt on my unit are fine. It's a total loss over one electronic part the manufacturer stopped supporting. That's not bad luck that's a business model with an expiration date built in. My treadmill is going in the dumpster.

Before you buy from any brand, ask: How long will you stock replacement consoles and control boards? Do you have an authorized technician in my zip code today? What's the warranty on a replacement part?

NordicTrack failed all three. Buy something else.

2\. The X24 Treadmill: A Cacophony of Incompetence

It was only after another 20 phone calls and escalating to management—who seem to avoid speaking with customers at all costs—that their engineering team finally diagnosed the problem. I would also observe that Nordic Track as we knew it — high-end equipment manufacturer — no longer exists. [**I bought a $2,000 treadmill (T 8.5 S)…**](https://www.trustpilot.com/reviews/69bdb12341e8a3f1e295cce1)

I bought a $2,000 treadmill (T 8.5 S) back in April 2024, and while the machine itself is decent quality, the company’s business model is incredibly frustrating. This was a massive purchase for me, and I was so excited to get it set up, but the experience has been a huge letdown.

The biggest issue is the paywall. This company expects you to drop a couple thousand dollars on a piece of equipment and then hit you with a mandatory $40/month iFIT subscription just to use the basic features of the screen. If you don't pay that $500-a-year "membership," you are locked out of almost everything, except the basic obvious features of speed and incline. You can't even set up your own custom interval workouts or use the streaming apps they recently added. It feels wrong to spend that much on a product only to have the hardware held hostage by a subscription.

I also found their transparency to be pretty poor. I tried to leave a review on their official website a week after my purchase, but the model was already delisted and there was no clear way to provide feedback. It feels like once they have your money, they aren't interested in what you have to say.

Even the design shows a lack of thought for the user, for example, the fan on my model isn't adjustable, so at my height, it’s completely useless. For a premium brand, you’d expect better ergonomics and at least some basic "smart" features included for free.

[**Still going strong after 4 years of ownership.**](https://www.trustpilot.com/reviews/6997bf70bfd52f1f3a3dc9c8)

It’s been an up-and-down journey over the last four years with my NordicTrack x32i treadmill and NordicTrack bike—but today, I can confidently say it’s been worth it.

When I first brought them home, I was blown away. The large, immersive screens and the world-class iFIT instructors instantly elevated my workouts. The trainers are truly best-in-class—engaging, motivating, and incredible storytellers. They take you around the world while pushing you to be better, and they genuinely make you want to get on your treadmill or bike multiple times a week.

There was a stretch—about a year—where I experienced frustrating shutdown issues with my treadmill. Workouts would cut off mid-session, and it tested my patience. I went through multiple troubleshooting steps, from upgrading my WiFi hardware to reinstalling software and applying firmware updates. It wasn’t easy. But once everything was resolved, the experience returned to being seamless and reliable. Since then, my workouts have been smooth and consistent.

The only other area that could impact a star rating is the subscription cost. To unlock the full power of the machine, you need the iFIT membership, and it is an investment—comparable to some gym memberships. While you can still use the treadmill without it (and I’ll say, the cushioning is excellent and easy on the knees, with solid metric tracking), you miss the immersive, motivating experience that truly makes this equipment special.

Last year, when I was considering canceling, I received a call from an iFIT representative, Jonah G. That call changed everything. He offered me a rate that made the subscription much more affordable and followed up to make sure I was enjoying the service. I’ve honestly never experienced that level of proactive, thoughtful customer service. Jonah also introduced me to a heart rate monitor promotion, which has been a complete game changer for my motivation and performance. His support made a real difference—thank you, Jonah!

With everything considered, I give NordicTrack and the iFIT subscription 5 stars. If you struggle with motivation, consistency, physical health, or even mental health, this setup can be transformational. Whether your goal is to walk your first mile or train for a marathon, there are structured programs that will guide you, push you, and help you stay accountable.

For me, it’s more than just equipment—it’s become a long-term investment in my health and I wanted to share my experience. I hope it helps those of you out there trying to decide if these products are right for you.

-Dave G-
